meta.title: Gross income and exclusions
meta.summary: The all-inclusive definition of gross income, when and to whom income is taxed, common types of income, Social Security benefits, and the main exclusions and fringe benefits.

videos.title: What counts as gross income?
videos.take: Gross income is all realized income from whatever source, unless the Code excludes it

scenes.say: The Code doesn't list what's taxable. It says everything is, unless something says otherwise. Here's how gross income works.

sub: All income from whatever source derived,
scenes.say: Section 61 defines gross income as all income from whatever source derived. That's deliberately broad: wages, tips, business profits, rent, prizes, even illegal income.

scenes.heading: Income is taxed when it is
items: An accession to wealth: you are better off
Not excluded or deferred by the Code
scenes.say: Income is taxed when it's an accession to wealth, when it's been realized through a transaction, when it isn't just getting your own money back, and when no provision excludes or defers it.
Realization matters. If Jake's shares rise by $5,000 this year, he's wealthier, but there's no income until he sells. That's why gains can be deferred for decades.
And getting back your own money isn't income. If Jake sells shares that cost $3,000 for $5,000, only the $2,000 gain is income. The $3,000 is a return of capital.

opts: Ruth gets back a $1,000 loan she made to a friend
Leo's savings account balance grows from deposits
scenes.say: Quick check. Which of these is gross income? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B. The prize is realized and makes Nora wealthier. The house hasn't been sold, the loan repayment is a return of capital, and deposits are Leo's own money.

videos.title: When, and to whom, income is taxed
videos.take: Cash-method taxpayers report income when received or constructively received; income is taxed to whoever earns it

scenes.say: Two questions follow every dollar of income. In which year is it taxed? And who pays the tax on it?

scenes.heading: Accounting methods
scenes.say: Almost all individuals use the cash method: income is taxed when it's received. Larger businesses use the accrual method: income is taxed when it's earned, whether or not the cash has arrived.

scenes.heading: Cash-method rules
items: Constructive receipt: available to you counts
Cash equivalents: checks and property count
Claim of right: income you hold, even if disputed
Prepaid income: generally taxed when received
scenes.say: Cash-method taxpayers still face rules. Income available to you is constructively received. A check or property counts as cash. Money you receive under a claim of right is taxed now, even if you might have to repay it. And prepaid income is generally taxed when received.

sub: Service income: taxed to the earner
Property income: taxed to the owner
scenes.say: On the question of who, income from services is taxed to the person who did the work. Income from property is taxed to whoever owns the property. To shift investment income, you have to give away the property itself.

Nine states, including California and Texas, use community property rules, which split most income earned during marriage equally between spouses. Minnesota is a common-law state, so each spouse owns what they earn.

scenes.q: On December 31, 2026 Nora's client says, 'Your $1,200 check is at the front desk.' Nora collects it on January 2. When is it income?
scenes.say: Quick check. On December thirty-first, a client tells Nora her twelve hundred dollar check is at the front desk. She picks it up on January second. When is it income? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's A, 2026. The check was available to her without restriction, so she constructively received it on December thirty-first.

videos.title: Common types of income
videos.take: Wages, tips, business and rental income, investment income, prizes, unemployment and forgiven debt are all taxable

scenes.say: Most income is easy to spot. Some is less obvious. Here's a tour of the common types, including a few that surprise people.

scenes.heading: Clearly taxable
scenes.say: Wages, bonuses and tips are taxable, as are business, rental and farm profits, interest, dividends and capital gains. So is unemployment compensation.

scenes.heading: Less obvious, still taxable
items: Barter: the value of what you receive
scenes.say: Less obvious: prizes and gambling winnings are taxable. If you trade services, the value of what you receive is income. If a lender forgives a debt, the forgiven amount is generally income. And illegal income is taxable too, which is how Al Capone went to prison in 1931.

scenes.heading: Alimony
scenes.say: Alimony depends on the date of the divorce. For divorces finalized before 2019, the payer deducts alimony and the recipient includes it. For divorces in 2019 or later, neither does. Child support is never income or deductible.
Income is taxable whether or not you get a W-2 or a 1099. Cash jobs, barter and payments through apps must all be reported.

scenes.q: Nora photographs a plumber's wedding in exchange for $1,500 of plumbing work. What does she report?
opts: Only if the plumber sends a 1099
scenes.say: Quick check. Nora photographs a plumber's wedding in exchange for fifteen hundred dollars of plumbing work. What does she report? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B. Barter income is the fair value of what she receives: $1,500.

videos.title: Taxing Social Security benefits
videos.take: Up to 85% of Social Security benefits are taxable, depending on provisional income

scenes.say: Are Social Security benefits taxable? Sometimes. It depends on a figure called provisional income.
Provisional income is your AGI without the benefits, plus tax-exempt interest, plus half of your Social Security benefits.

scenes.heading: Provisional income thresholds
scenes.say: For a single filer, benefits start to be taxable above $25,000 of provisional income, and up to eighty-five percent can be taxable above $34,000. For joint filers the thresholds are $32,000 and $44,000. These thresholds have never been indexed for inflation.

scenes.heading: Ruth's neighbor Gary, single
scenes.say: Gary is single, with a $20,000 pension and $24,000 of Social Security. His provisional income is $32,000. That's between the two thresholds, so the taxable amount is the lesser of half his benefits or half the excess over $25,000: $3,500.
Ruth's provisional income is only $16,800, her IRA withdrawals plus half her benefits, so none of her Social Security is taxable.

scenes.q: A single retiree has provisional income of $20,000. How much of her benefits is taxable?
scenes.say: Quick check. A single retiree has provisional income of twenty thousand dollars. How much of her benefits is taxable? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's A, none. She's below the $25,000 threshold.

videos.title: Exclusions
videos.take: Gifts, inheritances, life insurance, municipal interest and qualified scholarships are excluded from gross income

scenes.say: Exclusions are income the Code lets you leave out entirely. Here are the ones you'll meet most often.

scenes.heading: Common exclusions
items: Life insurance paid on a death
Gain on selling your home, up to a limit
scenes.say: Gifts and inheritances are excluded, though income they later earn is taxable. So are life insurance proceeds paid on a death, interest on state and local bonds, damages for physical injury or sickness, and most gain on selling your home, which we'll cover in Lecture 14.

Scholarships are excluded only to the extent they pay for tuition, required fees, books and supplies. Amounts for room and board are taxable. And payment for services, like a teaching assistantship, is wages.

scenes.heading: Sam's $6,000 SMSU scholarship
scenes.say: Sam gets a $6,000 scholarship. $5,200 covers tuition and fees and $500 his required books, so $5,700 is excluded. The remaining $300 goes toward his dorm room, and that's taxable income.
One more: US citizens who live and work abroad can exclude up to $132,900 of foreign earned income in 2026.

scenes.q: Ruth inherits shares worth $40,000 and receives $600 of dividends on them. What is her gross income?
scenes.say: Quick check. Ruth inherits shares worth forty thousand dollars and then receives six hundred dollars of dividends on them. What's her gross income? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's B. The inheritance is excluded, but the dividends it earns are taxable: $600.

videos.title: Fringe benefits
videos.take: Many employer-provided benefits are tax-free, which makes them worth more than equal cash pay

scenes.say: A dollar of health insurance from your employer can be worth more than a dollar of salary. Here's why fringe benefits matter.

scenes.heading: Tax-free fringe benefits
items: Health insurance and group-term life to $50,000
Parking and transit, up to $340 a month
scenes.say: Common tax-free fringes include employer health insurance and group-term life insurance up to $50,000, no-additional-cost services like an airline's empty seats, employee discounts, work tools, small de minimis perks, parking and transit up to $340 a month, and dependent care assistance up to $7,500 in 2026.

scenes.heading: Jake: $6,000 of health insurance
scenes.say: Jake's employer pays $6,000 of his family's health insurance. If he got that as salary instead, he'd pay twelve percent income tax and seven point six five percent payroll tax: $1,179. As a fringe benefit, it's tax-free.

sub: Many fringes must be offered broadly,
scenes.say: To be tax-free, many fringe benefits must be offered to employees broadly, not just to owners and highly paid executives.
A cafeteria plan lets employees choose between cash and benefits without being taxed on the choice. Health flexible spending accounts are capped at $3,400 for 2026.

scenes.q: Which benefit is taxable to Jake?
scenes.say: Quick check. Which benefit is taxable to Jake? Pause and pick.
scenes.reveal: It's C. Cash and gift cards are never de minimis, however small. The life cover, the turkey and the parking are tax-free.

warmup: Your grandmother gives you $1,000 for your birthday, and your employer gives you a $1,000 bonus. Are they taxed the same way?
No: the gift is excluded and the bonus is wages. Use it to introduce the all-inclusive definition and exclusions.
acts: Income or not? (a) Finding $500 cash in a used couch. (b) A $2,000 increase in a 401(k) balance. (c) A tax refund of Minnesota income tax deducted last year. (d) Frequent-flyer miles earned on personal travel.
(a) Income (treasure trove). (b) Not yet: deferred. (c) Income under the tax benefit rule if deducted with a benefit. (d) IRS doesn't tax personal-use miles.
A landlord receives, in December 2026, January 2027 rent of $1,500 and a refundable security deposit of $1,500. What is 2026 income?
$1,500: prepaid rent is taxed when received. The refundable deposit is not income while it may be returned.
A bank cancels $8,000 of a solvent taxpayer's credit card debt. What is the tax effect?
$8,000 of gross income from discharge of debt (Form 1099-C), unless an exclusion such as insolvency applies.
Married retirees: pension $30,000, Social Security $28,000, municipal interest $4,000. Compute provisional income and the taxable benefits.
Sam's roommate gets a $10,000 scholarship: $7,000 tuition, $600 books, $2,400 housing. He also earns $3,000 as a lab assistant. Gross income?
Rank these by after-tax value to Jake (12% income tax, 7.65% payroll): $1,000 cash, $1,000 of health insurance, $1,000 of dependent care assistance.
Health insurance and dependent care are worth $1,000; cash is worth about $803.
case: Ruth Lindqvist, 68, widowed, lives in Tracy on $24,000 of Social Security and $4,800 of IRA withdrawals. Suppose that in 2026 she also earns $900 of interest on a CD and $400 on Minnesota municipal bonds, inherits $30,000 from her sister, receives $10,000 of life insurance on her sister's death, and wins $1,200 at a casino.
How much of her Social Security is taxable?
List what is excluded and what is included.
Does she still qualify as Jake's dependent?

Provisional: 4,800 + 900 + 1,200 + 400 (muni) + 12,000 = 19,300 < 25,000, so benefits are not taxable. Included: IRA 4,800, interest 900, gambling 1,200 = 6,900. Excluded: inheritance, life insurance, muni interest, benefits. Gross income $6,900 is over $5,300, so she no longer qualifies as Jake's dependent: the casino win cost Jake a $500 credit.
exam: Explain the realization principle and the return-of-capital principle, with an example of each.

Income is taxed only when realized in a transaction (unsold shares that rise are not taxed). Recovering your investment is not income (sale for $5,000 of shares costing $3,000 gives $2,000 of income).
A single taxpayer has a pension of $18,000, tax-exempt interest of $2,000 and Social Security of $20,000. Compute the taxable Social Security.
outcomes: Apply the all-inclusive definition of gross income
Decide when and to whom income is taxed
Identify common and less obvious income
Apply the main exclusions, including scholarships
Explain the tax value of fringe benefits
take: Cash-method income is taxed when received or available
Barter, prizes, forgiven debt and illegal income are taxable
Up to 85% of benefits are taxable, by provisional income
Scholarships are tax-free only for tuition, fees and books
Tax-free fringes are worth more than equal cash

ex.q: Included in gross income or excluded?
items: Life insurance received on a death
ex.why: Section 61 includes everything unless a specific exclusion applies.

ex.q: Which concept means shares that rise in value are not taxed until sold?
ex.why: Income is recognized only when realized in a transaction.

ex.q: A cash-method dentist receives $3,000 in December 2026 for work in January 2027. When is it income?
ex.why: Prepaid income is generally taxed when received by a cash-method taxpayer.

ex.q: Match each divorce payment to its tax treatment.
pairs: Deducted by payer, income to recipient
ex.why: The TCJA changed alimony for divorces executed after 2018.

ex.q: A single retiree has a pension of $22,000 and Social Security of $16,000 (no tax-exempt interest). How much of the benefits is taxable?
A student's $8,000 scholarship pays $6,500 tuition, $400 books and $1,100 housing. How much is taxable?
ex.why: Only tuition, fees, books and supplies are excluded; housing is taxable.

items: Employer pays an employee's personal car loan
ex.why: Cash equivalents and personal expenses paid by an employer are wages.

ex.q: Jake gets $2,000 more salary instead of $2,000 of dependent care assistance. At 12% income tax and 7.65% payroll tax, how much less is the salary worth after tax?
